summary: Kaniksu NF L-4 cab on Fisher Peak, Boundary County; built 1930 or 1937 per conflicting sources; gone by 1964; Trail #27 reaches the saddle below the summit today.

facts.design: L-4 cab on four-foot concrete piers, atop the summit's northernmost point
facts.status_note: Gone by 1964 on both lookout pages. The Forest Service trail page says the lookout has long since disappeared.

access.note: Fisher Peak Trail #27, about 7 miles to the summit, listed for mid-June to November, subject to weather

visit.trail_note: Parking is limited to turnouts near the trailhead, about 5.5 miles along Trout Creek Road #634.

events.note: Newspapers reported plans for a new station on Fisher Peak, one of three new lookouts the Forest Service contemplated.
Firelookout.com dates the L-4 cab to 1930; the Idaho Fire Lookouts page gives 1937.
Lloyd Hydorn, the first staffer named on both pages.
Howard Monks Jr.; the Idaho page adds Randall Bearse as an assistant that year.
David Pace, the last named staffer.
Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 1937 for the L-4 cab; the same page's staff list begins in 1931.
Listed as gone by 1964 on both pages; the sources do not say how it ended.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com gives 1930 for the L-4 cab; the Idaho Fire Lookouts page gives 1937, though its own staff list starts in 1931. The record keeps 1930 as the earlier date and reports both.
The 1929 newspaper items describe a planned station, not a finished one, so the record does not use them as the build date.

notes_for_editor: Two lookout pages disagree on the build year (1930 vs 1937). The Bonners Ferry Herald items the Idaho page cites were not read directly. Access is listed as public because Trail #27 is a listed Forest Service trail; re-check the trail page before relying on it. The Forest Service trail page is the only current-day source.
